decisions.name: Theorem 12.2 (identity words are r.e.)
decisions.reason: Not a prerequisite for fixed undecidability. The displayed conjugate-of-products enumeration is inadequate for the full normal closure; do not import it as a proof.
decisions.evidence: The owned endpoint reduces the fixed recognizer directly through thm-fixed-finite-semigroup-has-undecidable-terminal-equality and thm-novikov-boone-undecidability-of-the-word-problem; neither proof enumerates all identity words or invokes Theorem 12.2.

decisions.name: Lemma 5 and Definition 6 (modular subgroups and rule extension)
decisions.reason: Specific subgroups of Z^2 * Z are unnecessary for the direct Boone presentation and cannot replace its associated-subgroup proof.
decisions.evidence: The manifest uses the explicitly presented Boone base groups and associated subgroups in lem-boone-base-groups-and-associated-free-bases and lem-boone-hnn-tower-and-auxiliary-subgroups; no modular subgroup or rule-extension construction occurs in the owned route.

decisions.name: Definition 3 and Theorem 4 (modular machines and undecidable halting set)
decisions.reason: Different machine compiler and arithmetic encoding; the assigned scope retains the explicit tape-machine/semigroup compiler.
decisions.evidence: lem-normalized-fixed-halting-machine-for-boone-simulation compiles the already published fixed recognizable HALT language to the required tape machine. The alternate modular-machine encoding is not an actual prerequisite.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.5
decisions.reason: Unrecognizable subsets of the naturals are not needed; the input language here is recognizable.
decisions.evidence: The reduction starts from the published recognizable but undecidable fixed HALT language; no unrecognizable set is selected or used by any owned item.

decisions.name: Definition 2 (good subgroup)
decisions.reason: Modular-machine subgroup machinery is specific to the alternate Aanderaa–Cohen proof; it is not substituted for Boone positive reconstruction.
decisions.evidence: The direct Boone proof supplies its own free-basis and HNN-associated-subgroup lemmas. Simpson's good-subgroup predicate belongs only to the declined modular-machine route and has no load-bearing use here.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.2
decisions.reason: Abelian normal forms supply a different decidable class; they are not used in the simulation proof.
decisions.evidence: No owned statement concerns decidability for abelian presentations; the construction proceeds through a machine semigroup and a fixed Boone HNN presentation.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.8
decisions.reason: General union/intersection closure is not used by the direct computable reduction.
decisions.evidence: The final contradiction composes a hypothetical fixed word-problem decider with one explicit computable map e to W(e); no general union or intersection closure theorem for recognizable sets is used.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.3
decisions.reason: Closure of solvable word problem under products is not needed to construct the counterexample.
decisions.evidence: Products of groups with solvable word problem do not enter the Boone presentation, its HNN normal-form analysis, or the fixed reduction endpoint.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.9
decisions.reason: Boolean closure of recursive sets is replaced by composing the alleged decider with the explicit encoding.
decisions.evidence: The proof uses the published undecidability of fixed HALT and an explicit many-one reduction. It does not form Boolean combinations of recursive sets.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.10
decisions.reason: Product encodings for arbitrary recursive subsets of naturals are not used by the fixed word compiler.
decisions.evidence: The compiler maps each single code e directly to one configuration word and then one special group word; no product coding of arbitrary subsets of the naturals is used.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.7
decisions.reason: A one-input looping example is not needed; rejecting branches are sent to an explicit loop in the compiler.
decisions.evidence: Rejecting branches are totalized to a fixed explicit nonhalting loop inside lem-normalized-fixed-halting-machine-for-boone-simulation. The source's separate toy looping example supplies no premise of that construction.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.6
decisions.reason: The parity language is a decidable toy machine, unrelated to the required fixed undecidable recognizer.
decisions.evidence: The owned compiler begins with a fixed recognizer for HALT_TM and preserves its accepting runs. A separate decidable parity machine is neither an example requested by the B page nor a proof prerequisite.

decisions.name: Every doubly infinite tape TM has an equivalent left-bounded TM
decisions.reason: Two-sided tape folding changes the representation and is outside the commissioned stay-put normal form; this theorem is not used in its proof.
decisions.evidence: The batch-12 theorem changes only S moves of the right-infinite one-tape model already fixed by its hypotheses, via a two-step R/L macro. It never folds a two-sided tape or uses the declined representation theorem.

decisions.name: Remark 9 (prescribed r.e. degree)
decisions.reason: Exact Turing-degree realization is stronger than this fixed-undecidability endpoint and is only cited, not proved, in this paper.
decisions.evidence: The commissioned endpoint is undecidability for one fixed finite presentation, proved by the explicit HALT reduction. Prescribing an arbitrary r.e. Turing degree is strictly stronger and no owned claim asserts it.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.4
decisions.reason: Inheritance by finitely generated subgroups is not used; this proof constructs a group directly.
decisions.evidence: The owned construction builds its fixed group presentation directly and never transfers decidability or undecidability along finitely generated subgroup inclusion.

decisions.name: Exercise 12.1
decisions.reason: Finite-group lookup tables are already an independent decidable class; no use in the Boone construction.
decisions.evidence: Finite-group lookup is unrelated to the constructed infinite HNN tower and supplies no premise for either direction of the Boone special-word equivalence.

decisions.name: Lemma 7 (halting-history generated subgroup)
decisions.reason: Its modular-machine invariant is not the Boone special-word invariant required on this page.
decisions.evidence: The owned reverse implication is lem-boone-positive-history-reconstruction, using the specific Boone positive-word invariant and Britton analysis. Simpson's modular-machine history subgroup is a different invariant and is not imported.
